title: The Use of Ginger Bioactive Compounds in Pregnancy: An Evidence Scan and Umbrella Review of Existing Meta-Analyses
quick: Ginger may reduce nausea; vomiting and comparison with vitamin B6 less certain.
details: 7 meta-analyses; 4 critically low, 3 low AMSTAR-2; none reported funding of component trials; overlapping RCTs.
funding: Gates Foundation INV-047386; identified ginger topic, otherwise no analysis/writing/publication restrictions per authors
verification: Original HTML methods, results, Figure 3, funding/COI
limitations: Not independent trials; mild nausea not hyperemesis; component funding supplement remains unextracted

title: Plant-derived complementary therapies for nausea and vomiting of pregnancy: a systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
population: 28 RCTs 2798 participants; nausea up to 20 weeks
quick: Ginger and B6 may both help nausea; no clear best plant remedy.
details: VAS network 7 trials 594; ginger MD -2.06, B6 -1.89 versus placebo, low confidence. PUQE network inconsistent and uninterpretable. 11/28 trials report at least one adverse event; others vary in completeness.
funding: No external funding; Srinakharinwirot University medical center publication support; no funder role declared
verification: Original publisher abstract, funding, COI; Oct 17 2026; CRD420251116302
limitations: Different symptom scales; no clinical ranking, no proof safety; overlap P7-01

title: A systematic review and meta-analysis of the effect and safety of ginger in the treatment of pregnancy-associated nausea and vomiting
quick: Nausea benefit more convincing than vomiting benefit.
details: Vomiting result MD .72 (-.03 to 1.46), I2 71%; scale direction requires full text.
limitations: Low quality, overlaps P7-01; hold numeric vomiting chart until coding confirmed

title: The Management of Nausea and Vomiting in Pregnancy and Hyperemesis Gravidarum (Green-top Guideline No. 69)
quick: Severe vomiting needs effective medical care, not more home remedies.
details: Guideline cautions against suggesting ginger to patients presenting for medical help for HG because of possible delay.
funding: Professional guideline; panel COI not extracted
limitations: Do not extrapolate HG advice to all mild nausea; medical escalation visible

title: Is oral consumption of dates in the peripartum period effective and safe integrative care to facilitate childbirth and improve perinatal outcomes: a comprehensive revised systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis
quick: Dates may help certain labor outcomes, but the evidence has limitations.
details: 4/15 RCTs low RoB; late pregnancy gestation MD -1.97 days (3 RCTs,1 non-RCT); in-labor active phase MD -88.38 min (3 RCTs). Different timing; sparse safety.
funding: Abadan University of Medical Sciences Religion, Health and Technology Studies Center grant 1538; no funder role reported
verification: Original HTML methods, Figs 1–2, RoB, funding and declarations; CRD42023399626
limitations: Primary funding not audited; some outcomes sensitive to study exclusion; no induction or dose protocol, glycemic considerations

title: Biophysical effects, safety and efficacy of raspberry leaf use in pregnancy: a systematic integrative review
quick: Raspberry leaf has a tradition of use, but reliable clinical benefit and safety are not established.
details: Sparse human evidence; distinguish leaf tea/extract, lab uterine effects and clinical outcomes.
financial_ties: First author conducting raspberry leaf observational PhD study; not financial tie
limitations: No automatic late-pregnancy schedule; no extrapolation from isolated tissue

title: Castor oil, bath and/or enema for cervical priming and induction of labour
quick: Castor oil is not a proven safe home induction method.
details: Small trials, uncertain efficacy; nausea common.
limitations: Older evidence; no instruction or dose

title: Inducing labour — recommendations
quick: Do not use home remedies to replace an induction plan.
details: Evidence does not support castor oil, herbal supplements and other specified methods for induction.
limitations: UK jurisdiction; respect clinician plan and urgent fetal warning signs

title: Cephalic version by moxibustion for breech presentation
quick: Moxibustion may reduce breech positioning at birth, but has not clearly reduced cesarean births.
details: Usual care comparison RR .87 (.78–.99) non-cephalic at birth; C-section .94 (.83–1.05); harms poorly reported.
verification: Original official abstract outcomes and harms
limitations: No DIY heat/smoke technique, no delay to assessment or ECV; review includes prior trials

title: Moxibustion did not have an effect in a randomised clinical trial for version of breech position
quick: A separate trial did not find a benefit.
details: Null result; exact sample and estimates pending.
verification: Indexed primary abstract; direct open blocked
limitations: Not proof no protocol works; cohort membership P7-09 to verify

title: Moxibustion for Correction of Breech Presentation: A Randomized Controlled Trial
quick: An earlier trial reported favorable fetal positioning outcomes.
details: Randomized intervention and control; numerical extraction deferred.
limitations: Not independent of review; no technique instructions

title: Continuous support for women during childbirth
quick: A supportive person during labor may improve birth experience and some birth outcomes.
details: Spontaneous vaginal birth RR 1.08; C-section RR .75; negative experience RR .69; low certainty for these endpoints.
funding: Review and underlying trial funding not extracted
limitations: Unblinded intervention; varied care settings, companion type and policies; no guaranteed vaginal birth

title: Massage, reflexology and other manual methods for managing pain in labour
quick: Massage may help comfort if the mother wants it.
details: Variable small trials; not established method to avoid medical pain relief.
limitations: Consent and clinical circumstances; no standardized dose

title: Relaxation techniques for pain management in labour
quick: Breathing, relaxation and music may help coping.
details: Mixed interventions and uncertain evidence; no birth-mode guarantee.
limitations: Separate yoga eligibility and medical analgesia

title: Acupuncture or acupressure for pain management during labour
quick: Some trials suggest better pain relief satisfaction, but results depend on comparison.
details: Sham comparison satisfaction RR 2.38; pharmacological analgesia RR .75. Acupressure vs combined control SMD -.42.
limitations: No needle or pressure-point instruction; clinical analgesia always available

title: Aromatherapy for Labour Pain Management: Umbrella Review
quick: Some aroma studies suggest pain relief, but confidence is low.
details: Reviews and trials have limitations, safety reporting incomplete; older Cochrane insufficient.
limitations: No ingestion or undiluted oils; not infant exposure recommendation; NICE differs

title: Intrapartum care — recommendations
quick: Breathing, warm bath/shower and massage may help early labor.
details: NICE advises not offering aromatherapy, yoga or acupressure for latent-stage pain relief; respect patient choice within care plan.
limitations: Jurisdiction and phase specific; not a ban on all yoga

title: Immersion in water in labour and birth
quick: Water immersion may reduce epidural use, not clearly change delivery mode.
details: Spontaneous vaginal birth RR 1.01 (.97–1.04), cesarean 1.27 (.91–1.79).
limitations: Laboring in water distinct from underwater delivery; clinical eligibility

title: Hypnosis for pain management during labour and childbirth
quick: Hypnosis may help some people cope; evidence very uncertain.
details: Pharmacological pain relief RR .73 (.57–.94), 8 studies 2916, very low certainty.
limitations: No pressure to avoid analgesia; no commercial class superiority

title: Effect of Acupuncture vs Sham Acupuncture on Live Births Among Women Undergoing In Vitro Fertilization: A Randomized Clinical Trial
population: 848 randomized IVF participants; 809 live birth data
quick: Acupuncture did not clearly increase live births in this trial.
financial_ties: NICM accepts industry donations; author shares in IVF/fertility companies, Johnson pharmaceutical fees/support, Smith acupuncture clinic collaboration; not direct acupuncture manufacturer sponsor
verification: Original PubMed abstract and COI, indexed JAMA funding; ACTRN12611000226909
limitations: Separate clinical pregnancy from live birth; no substitution for fertility care

title: Acupuncture versus placebo acupuncture for in vitro fertilisation: a systematic review and meta-analysis
quick: Pooled evidence does not establish more live births.
details: Live birth RR .87 (.75–1.01), 4 RCTs 1835, high certainty per authors.
limitations: Overlap P7-20; no independent count

title: Timing and dose of acupuncture as adjuncts to assisted reproduction: a meta-analysis and model-based network meta-analysis
quick: Some pregnancy measures improved, but live-birth benefit remained unclear.
details: Clinical pregnancy RR 1.25 (1.14–1.37), live birth RR 1.14 (.98–1.32).
limitations: Mixed comparators and model assumptions; not proof of optimal dose or live births

title: Oral galactagogues (natural therapies or drugs) for increasing breast milk production in mothers of non-hospitalised term infants
quick: Herbal milk boosters have inconsistent results.
details: Milk volume I2=99%, not pooled; safety and longer-term breastfeeding evidence uncertain.
limitations: Herbs/products not interchangeable; feeding assessment first

title: The effect of Moringa oleifera capsule in increasing breast milk volume in early postpartum patients: A double-blind, randomized controlled trial
quick: Moringa did not clearly increase early milk volume in this trial.
details: Day 3 median 73.5 vs50 mL, p=.19; authors nevertheless emphasize descriptive 47% difference; mostly cesarean deliveries.
funding: Chulalongkorn University Ratchadaphiseksomphot Endowment Fund and Placental related diseases Research Unit
verification: Original HTML methods, results, limitations, acknowledgement and COI
limitations: Do not treat 47% descriptive ratio as proven effect; no comparison of long-term outcome extracted; no supplement dose

title: Moringa oleifera Supplementation as a Natural Galactagogue: A Systematic Review on Its Role in Supporting Milk Volume and Prolactin Levels
quick: Some studies report benefits but reliable infant outcomes and safety need more research.
details: Review reports increases in milk volume and prolactin; heterogeneity and trial membership pending.
limitations: Prolactin surrogate; check P7-24 overlap; no pooled prescription

title: Fenugreek
quick: Fenugreek may cause side effects and has inconsistent milk-supply evidence.
details: LactMed summarizes conflicting reviews and self-reported adverse reactions.
limitations: Allergy/interactions and formulations; not a substitute for feeding assessment

title: Breastfeeding Challenges
quick: Check feeding, latch and infant growth before trying milk boosters.
details: Galactagogues should not be first-line therapy; assess causes.
funding: Professional guideline; panel COI not audited
limitations: No infant hydration or milk adequacy judged by pump volume alone

title: Information about Domperidone
quick: Domperidone has serious risks and is not approved in the US for increasing milk supply.
details: Cardiac risk; withdrawal-related neuropsychiatric signal.
limitations: No acquisition, self-dosing or abrupt cessation advice; clinician help

title: Effects from a single application of photobiomodulation on pain intensity from perineal trauma related to childbirth: A randomized controlled trial
population: 60 immediate postpartum women with perineal trauma
quick: One red/infrared light session was not better than sham.
details: 30-min pain NRS 3.63 SD2.57 vs2.53 SD2.15, p=.089; no significant group-time interaction for pain/healing.
funding: No specific research grant declared; CAPES Brazil paid publication charge
verification: Original full HTML abstract, registration, funding and acknowledgements; U1111-1279-3594
limitations: Single parameters, immediate postpartum; no home dose; no general claim all light therapy ineffective

title: Photobiomodulation as a promising approach in the management of nipple lesions during breastfeeding: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials
quick: Light therapy may help nipple pain, but evidence certainty is low.
details: Sucking pain OR .43 (.23–.79); outcome definition and contributing n require primary table.
limitations: Do not equate nipple and perineal outcomes; no home device settings

title: Nonpharmacological Interventions for Treating Breastfeeding Nipple Pain: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
quick: Another review found uncertain pain benefit from light therapy.
details: MD -.15; indexed abstract interval has malformed lower value; do not repair by guessing.
limitations: Hold numeric interval; check overlap with P7-30; different outcomes

title: Low-level laser therapy for breastfeeding women with nipple pain in the early postpartum period: a randomized controlled trial
quick: Newer trial reports favorable pain diary results.
details: Pain lower at several time points; effect sizes and primary endpoint need extraction.
limitations: Online vs issue date separate; registration/overlap with P7-29 unresolved; no clinical prescription

title: Local cooling for relieving pain from perineal trauma sustained during childbirth
quick: Local cooling may help discomfort in the first two days; evidence uncertain.
details: Very low certainty; use clinician-directed comfort measures.
limitations: Do not apply ice directly to tissue or delay wound/infection assessment

title: Interventions for treating painful nipples among breastfeeding women
quick: No particular ointment or dressing had clear overall superiority.
details: Lanolin, expressed milk, glycerine and other products insufficient evidence; latch assessment important.
limitations: Older review; no medical treatment of infection; compare newer trials

title: An open single-arm clinical study of microneedle radiofrequency technology for addressing abdominal skin laxity in postpartum women
quick: Promising before/after results cannot separate treatment from natural recovery.
details: No concurrent control; detailed outcome and harms extraction pending.
verification: Indexed primary record; direct opening blocked
limitations: No pregnancy use, brand endorsement or claims of proven tightening

title: Reduction of abdominal skin laxity in women postvaginal delivery using the synergistic emission of radiofrequency and targeted pressure energies
quick: Reported improvement requires better controlled confirmation.
details: Device-specific effect; design and disclosure verification pending.
limitations: Natural postpartum recovery and vendor ties not yet disentangled

title: A Systematic Review on Treatment Outcomes of Striae
quick: Some procedures improve appearance, but complete resolution is not assured.
details: PRP complete response 4/13 striae rubra in aggregated reports; not a head-to-head success rate.
limitations: Small denominators, heterogeneity, mixed designs; no pregnancy treatment recommendation

title: Potential Risks with Certain Uses of Radiofrequency (RF) Microneedling – FDA Safety Communication
quick: RF microneedling has reported serious injuries.
details: Burns, scarring, fat loss, disfigurement and nerve damage reports; incidence unknown.
limitations: No home use, no pregnancy elective use, preserve previous hold

title: Effect of radiofrequency therapy in the treatment of de novo dyspareunia at 4 to 12 months postpartum: a randomized clinical trial
quick: New trial suggests possible pain benefit; evidence and device safety need review.
details: RF plus massage versus sham plus massage; indexed conclusion reports improvement.
verification: Indexed primary abstract; direct open blocked
limitations: Do not equate with cosmetic vaginal rejuvenation; no home or routine treatment recommendation

title: Treating infant colic with the probiotic Lactobacillus reuteri: double blind, placebo controlled randomised trial
quick: In this trial babies receiving probiotics cried or fussed more.
details: At month 1 adjusted mean difference +49 min/day (8–90); exclusively breastfed +19 (-49–87), n50.
funding: Australian NHMRC; BioGaia supplied active and placebo free; authors report no sponsor involvement in design, analysis, writing or publication
financial_ties: Tang and Heine Nestlé/Nutricia advisory/honoraria; Tang unrelated products from Nestlé and Dicofarm; other disclosures per primary article
verification: Indexed BMJ original funding, disclosures and results; direct opening 403/PMC captcha
limitations: Product-specific, adverse direction despite in-kind support; parent diary; included in P7-41

title: Lactobacillus reuteri to Treat Infant Colic: A Meta-analysis
quick: The same strain may help some breastfed infants; formula-fed evidence is insufficient.
details: Day 21 change -25.4 min/day (-47.3 to-3.5); success ratio 1.7 (1.4–2.2); breastfed NNT 2.6 (2–3.6).
financial_ties: Sung Mead Johnson fees; Tancredi Pfizer fees; Cabana/Szajewska BioGaia fees; Dupont Nutricia/Nestlé boards and others; Savino multiple nutrition/pharma ties; full primary statement linked
verification: Original PubMed abstract and extensive COI
limitations: Includes P7-40; not independent contradiction, different day/feeding populations; strain typo in abstract selection DSM17398 vs DSM17938 elsewhere; verify before import

title: Probiotics for infantile colic: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial investigating Lactobacillus reuteri DSM 17938
quick: One smaller trial found less crying.
details: Day 21 median 60 vs102 min/day; responder RR 3.3 (1.55–7.03).
limitations: Confirm analysis denominators; overlapping review P7-41; no broad probiotic recommendation

title: Probiotics to prevent necrotising enterocolitis in very preterm or very low birth weight infants
quick: Some preterm hospital studies suggest fewer serious bowel complications, but the smallest infants have less certain benefit.
details: NEC RR .54 (.46–.65) low certainty; mortality .77 (.66–.90) moderate; extremely preterm NEC .92 (.69–1.22).
limitations: Different strains/products; specialist NICU only; do not use as home advice; FDA alert P7-44

title: FDA Raises Concerns About Probiotic Products Sold for Use in Hospitalized Preterm Infants
quick: Probiotic organisms can sometimes cause serious infection in premature babies.
details: FDA reports invasive disease, one death in 2023 and other adverse-event reports; no incidence denominator.
limitations: No home administration, specialist care; no inference all probiotic food unsafe

title: Manipulative therapies for infantile colic
quick: Evidence for manipulation is weak; unblinded ratings can influence results.
details: Blinded assessment essential; harms poorly studied.
limitations: No spinal manipulation or cranial procedure directions

title: Exploring Manual Interventions for Infantile Colic: A Scoping Review of the Evidence
quick: Some gentle approaches may provide short-term relief; safety evidence is incomplete.
details: Multiple different therapies; objective measures and adverse event surveillance needed.
limitations: Massage not interchangeable with manipulation; no clinical safety guarantee

title: Spinal manipulation and mobilisation in paediatrics – an international evidence-based position statement for physiotherapists
quick: Do not use spinal manipulation or mobilization on infants.
details: Taskforce recommends against infant manipulation/mobilization; evidence insufficient for non-musculoskeletal uses.
funding: Professional specialty group initiative; funding not extracted
limitations: Not a prohibition on normal gentle holding or indicated pediatric PT

title: Pediatric massage therapy in infants and children under 5 years: An umbrella review of systematic reviews
quick: Massage may be a bonding activity, but research varies by age and condition.
details: Review of varied outcomes; effect extraction pending.
limitations: Prior P2-26 healthy infant review, no guaranteed developmental acceleration

title: The effectiveness of mother-led infant massage on symptoms of maternal postnatal depression: A systematic review
quick: Some research suggests bonding and mood benefits.
details: Maternal symptoms and interaction improved in reviewed studies; causal certainty pending.
limitations: Adjunct only, never replace mental health care

title: Effects of Human Maternal Placentophagy on Maternal Postpartum Iron Status: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Pilot Study
quick: Placenta capsules did not clearly improve iron status.
details: No significant iron benefit versus beef placebo in adequate dietary iron context.
limitations: Small sample; not anemia treatment

title: Notes from the Field: Late-Onset Infant Group B Streptococcus Infection Associated with Maternal Consumption of Capsules Containing Dehydrated Placenta — Oregon, 2016
population: Maternal placenta capsule use and infant infection
quick: Placenta processing may not kill harmful bacteria.
details: Identical sequenced GBS strains in infant and capsules; CDC advises avoidance.
limitations: Case cannot estimate frequency; avoid encapsulation guidance

title: Oral administration of maternal vaginal microbes at birth to restore gut microbiome development in infants born by caesarean section: A pilot randomised placebo-controlled trial
quick: One trial found no detectable gut microbiome benefit.
details: No composition/function difference at 1 or 3 months.
funding: Health Research Council of New Zealand, A Better Start National Science Challenge
limitations: Different delivery method than swabbing; no clinical efficacy

title: Effects of vaginal seeding on gut microbiota, body mass index, and allergy risks in infants born through cesarean delivery: a randomized clinical trial
quick: Another study did not show benefits for growth, microbiome or allergy risk through two years.
details: Null reported outcomes; follow-up and power details pending.
limitations: No home technique or infection safety inference

title: Effects of vaginal microbiota transfer on the neurodevelopment and microbiome of cesarean-born infants: A blinded randomized controlled trial
quick: A small trial found promising six-month developmental scores.
details: ASQ-3 score favorable; numerical effects, sample and adverse events require primary extraction.
limitations: Short follow-up, developmental screening score not IQ, infection risks and conflicting results

title: Maternal Bacterial Engraftment in Multiple Body Sites of Cesarean Section Born Neonates after Vaginal Seeding-a Randomized Controlled Trial
quick: Transfer can change certain early microbial measurements.
details: Skin/stool measurements at one day and one month.
funding: NIH NHLBI K01HL141589 among indexed grants; full list pending
limitations: Microbial surrogate not clinical benefit

title: Vaginal Seeding
quick: Vaginal seeding should remain within approved research.
details: Infectious exposure and insufficient safety/benefit evidence.
limitations: Recheck guidance date before release; no procedure instructions

title: Risks of Infectious Diseases in Newborns Exposed to Alternative Perinatal Practices
quick: Some traditional newborn practices can expose babies to infection.
details: Vaginal seeding not recommended outside research; other practices need clinical assessment.
limitations: Not all cultural practices unsafe; assess individual practice

title: Immediate Kangaroo Mother Care and Survival of Infants with Low Birth Weight
population: Hospitalized infants 1.0–1.799 kg in five countries
quick: Early supervised skin-to-skin care with feeding support can save lives in this population.
funding: Gates Foundation grant to WHO OPP1151718
limitations: Facility protocol and monitoring; not a substitute for neonatal care or safe sleep

title: Kangaroo mother care to reduce morbidity and mortality in low birthweight infants
quick: New review supports the role of kangaroo care; exact updated estimates need extraction.
details: Moderate certainty mortality and nosocomial infection per indexed abstract.
verification: Indexed primary abstract; direct open blocked
limitations: Do not assume old 2016 web-summary estimates belong to 2026 update; overlap P7-58

title: WHO recommendations for care of the preterm or low-birth-weight infant: Evidence and recommendations
quick: Kangaroo care is established neonatal care, not merely an alternative remedy.
details: Start as soon as possible with clinical context and monitoring.
limitations: Clinical team, safe positioning/airway, no sleeping caregiver with infant

title: Physical activity and perinatal depression and anxiety: a global umbrella review and meta-meta-analysis
quick: Yoga and other activity may help mood symptoms.
details: Yoga SMD -.55 (-.95 to-.15); mixed activity -.54 (-.70 to-.38).
limitations: Reviews overlap; SMD not percent; no substitute for mental health treatment

title: Effects of different types of exercise interventions on perinatal depression, anxiety, and quality of life: a systematic review and meta-analysis
quick: Benefits look smaller when comparison groups also receive support.
details: Active controls attenuate effect relative to no treatment.
limitations: Avoid simplistic ranking; clinical eligibility and mental health referrals

title: Herbal Products
quick: Food herbs and concentrated supplements are different exposures.
details: Products may contain variable ingredients, contaminants or interactions.
limitations: No blanket approval for herbal mixtures

title: Ashwagandha: Usefulness and Safety
quick: Avoid ashwagandha during pregnancy and breastfeeding.
details: NCCIH safety advice; interactions and liver injury concerns.
limitations: Do not substitute for prescribed care

title: Essential oils: Poisonous when misused
quick: Concentrated essential oils can poison children.
details: Ingestion, aspiration or skin overexposure risks; seek poison center guidance.
limitations: No ingestion, application or diffusion dosing for infants; emergency escalation

title: Foods and Drinks to Avoid or Limit
quick: No honey before 12 months because of botulism risk.
details: Do not add honey to food, formula, water or pacifiers.
limitations: No home remedy exceptions; no infant herbal tea replacement for feeds

title: Safely Soothing Teething Pain in Infants and Children
quick: Avoid risky teething products.
details: FDA warnings about benzocaine/lidocaine, homeopathic products and teething jewelry.
limitations: No necklaces or topical anesthetic instructions; pediatric guidance

title: Some Homeopathic Products May Put You at Risk
quick: Homeopathic labeling does not establish safety or efficacy.
details: No FDA-approved homeopathic product; manufacturing variability may cause toxic exposures.
limitations: No substitute for established preventive or medical care
